title: chargehand local profile, v1
description: Environment-specific settings. Your own lives in profiles/local.json (gitignored), and every field is optional (ADR 0026) — chargehand runs with none at all. Secrets are referenced by item name, never stored here.

runtime.description: Names the runtime to drive (ADR 0026); wins over CHARGEHAND_RUNTIME. Unset: the profile's only runtime block (opencode or claude_code) names it (ADR 0032); with none or both, PATH is probed for a known agent CLI — none found or more than one found is an error.

secrets.description: Ordered secret lookup (ADR 0026): the first source that resolves an item wins. Default with no profile: env only. A profile still carrying "secret_store": "keychain" needs the one-line migration to an explicit command entry shown in example.json.

env.description: Look up the item as an environment variable (uppercased, - to _).

command.description: Argv run directly via Process, no shell; "{item}" is substituted per array element.

url.description: The orchestrator's own OpenCode server, bound to loopback.

binary.description: Pinned OpenCode binary the launcher starts.

version.description: Expected /api/info version; the adapter refuses to run on a mismatch.

claude_code.description: Claude Code CLI as the worker runtime (ADR 0020). When set, it is used instead of opencode. At most one credential; with neither, the CLI's own signed-in login (--setting-sources "").

version.description: Expected `claude --version`; the adapter refuses to run on a mismatch.

api_key_secret.description: Secret item holding ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: per-token billing, workers run with --bare.

oauth_token_secret.description: Secret item holding a `claude setup-token` OAuth token: the owner's subscription limits, workers run with --setting-sources "".

base_url.description: Anthropic-compatible gateway the workers call (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL). Unset: Anthropic directly; an inherited ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is ignored.

custom_headers_secret.description: Secret item holding header lines (`Name: value`, one per line) the workers send to base_url as ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS, e.g. a gateway's virtual key. Needs base_url. Plain workers only: driven sessions do not use base_url.

worker_root.description: Where worker clones and worktrees live. Must be outside the OpenCode user's home: OpenCode discovers skills by walking up from the session directory. Default (ADR 0026): a fixed directory outside $HOME, created on first use.

signing.description: Sign every result (ADR 0036). Chargehand never creates or stores a key. CHARGEHAND_SIGNING_KEY_FILE overrides key_file.

key_file.description: A P-256 private key in PEM: openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout | openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -nocrypt -out signing-key.pem

support_check.description: Default true (ADR 0036): after a node, one call on the intake model judges whether the text each claim cites supports it; unsupported claims move to open_questions and the rest carry support. false: no check, no extra call.

sandbox.description: Where a writing preset's tests run (ADR 0035): the platform's sandbox, with no network and a cut environment unless allowed here.

kind.description: auto (default): sandbox-exec on macOS, bwrap on Linux, and a writing run is refused when neither is there. none: run the tests unconfined, an explicit opt-in.

network.description: Allow the sandboxed command network access. Default false; a build that restores packages needs true.

env.description: Names of environment variables passed to the command besides PATH, LANG, LC_ALL and TERM.

driven.description: Driven writing sessions (ADR 0039): each task runs in its own container and ends in a draft pull request. Off unless enabled.

max_parallel.description: Tasks running at once in one batch. Default 2. How many really run is governed by admission (memory, pressure, load) and the rate-limit pause.

max_parallel_total.description: Tasks running at once across batches. Default 4. The runner's --max-containers must allow them.

max_session_calls.description: Research and review runs that sessions may have executing at once, across all sessions. Default 2; with more sessions than this, a session's call waits for a slot.

images.description: Session images by digest; nothing else may run.

limits.description: Operational limits of a session's container, replacing the same keys of the driven preset's driven block (a key left out keeps the preset's value). Tuned here because a change to presets/driven.yaml needs Prompt CI; prompts and permissions stay in the preset.

max_minutes.description: Wall clock for one task's session.

no_progress_minutes.description: No stream event for this long ends the session as stalled.

max_turns.description: Assistant messages after which the session ends as stalled.

max_tokens.description: Input plus output tokens for one task.

max_continuations.description: Further sessions on the same branch after one is stopped by the turn limit or the wall clock with work committed (ADR 0044). Each gets max_turns and max_minutes again; max_tokens is shared. Default 2; 0: none.

planning.description: ADR 0049's planning step: before a batch starts, one cheap read-only run through the orchestrator sizes tasks that have no size (S, M, L), splits a large task into an ordered chain and gives tasks that would take the same next number (migrations, ADR files) their own. The caller's size and depends_on always win. The plan is the batch result's plan artifact. A request's driven.plan overrides enabled.

preset.description: The preset the run uses; it must be read-only. Default cheap.

learning.description: ADR 0045's learning loop: every finished task leaves a record (size class, budget, spend, stop reason, governor decisions, outcome) next to the run log, the server reads the outcome of its pull request back from the forge (merged unchanged, merged after edits, closed, open; off when no forge credential is configured), and chargehand learn report sums them up. A key left out keeps its default.

retro.description: After each batch, one cheap read-only run over the batch's records writes a short retro, the batch result's retro artifact. Default false.

retro_preset.description: The preset the retro run uses; it must be read-only. Default cheap.

pr_days.description: How long after a task finished its pull request is read again until it is merged or closed. Default 14.

pr_check_minutes.description: How often the server reads the pull requests that are still open. Default 60.

admission.description: ADR 0045's admission: a task starts only when the host's available memory minus reserve_mb covers the task's memory request (the 90th percentile of the peak memory that sessions of its repository used, else default_request_mb; never above the container's memory limit, never below 512 MiB), memory pressure is under max_memory_pressure and, when set, the load is under max_load_per_cpu. Running tasks are never stopped for it; with nothing of this server running, one task starts anyway.

reserve_mb.description: Memory left for everything else on the host. Default 1024.

max_load_per_cpu.description: A one-minute load average per processor above this holds new starts. Default: no load rule.

default_request_mb.description: The memory request of a task while fewer than 10 session peaks are recorded for its repository and for all repositories. Clamped to the container's memory limit. Default 1536.

max_memory_pressure.description: New starts wait while the host's memory pressure (Linux PSI, some avg10 of /proc/pressure/memory, in percent) is above this. A host without PSI skips the rule; 100 turns it off. Default 10.

services.description: ADR 0048: what a batch's containers share. Off unless a key is set. Needs a runner built from the same release, started with --service-images for services.

caches.description: Ecosystems whose package cache is a named volume per repository, mounted read-write into that repository's sessions and verifier at /cache/<ecosystem>.

images.description: A session image by ecosystem name (gradle, maven, ...), used when the repository has that ecosystem. Each value must also be in driven.images.

repositories.description: Per owner/repo: test services (a database) started on the batch network for the batch's lifetime.

name.description: The host name on the batch network.

image.description: By digest; the runner must list it in --service-images.

env.description: The service's environment: test values only, never a real secret.

tmpfs.description: Memory-backed directories of the image (a database's data directory).

note.description: One line the session reads next to the address.

governor.description: ADR 0045's governor in each session: deterministic stuck and spend signals with a warn-then-checkpoint ladder, logged to governor.jsonl. Profile keys because a change to presets/driven.yaml needs Prompt CI. A key left out keeps its default.

mode.description: observe (default): decisions are logged and none acted on; enforce: a checkpoint or a stop also ends the session, which leaves a handoff for the next one (a checkpoint continues, a spent budget is salvaged as a partial draft pull request); off: no governor.

budgets.description: Flat budget per size class in the dollar equivalent (tokens priced with prices, also on a subscription). Defaults S 1.5, M 4, L 10. Used until a size class has enough finished tasks for history.

history.description: ADR 0045's budget from history: once a size class has min_tasks finished tasks (completed, or stopped at their budget) in the last window_days days for the repository, or else for all repositories, its budget is the percentile-th percentile of their spend. Below that the flat budget applies; a task's own budget_usd always wins. A key left out keeps its default.

min_tasks.description: Finished tasks of the size class needed. Default 20.

window_days.description: How far back finished tasks count. Default 60.

percentile.description: Nearest-rank percentile of their spend. Default 80.

repeat_calls.description: Identical action and observation pairs in a row that fire repeated_call. Default 4.

repeat_failures.description: Failures of one identical action that fire repeated_failure. Default 3.

failing_calls.description: Failing tool calls in a row that fire failing_calls. Default 8.

probe_commands.description: environment_probing fires on the command after this many that only ask what the container has. Default 10.

no_growth_turns.description: Turns with the diff's line count unchanged that fire no_diff_growth. Default 40.

rewarn_turns.description: A signal firing again at least this many turns after its warn is a checkpoint. Default 10.

context_tokens.description: One message's context above this is a checkpoint. Default 160000.

checkpoint_at.description: Share of the budget at which spend is a checkpoint; 100% is a stop. Default 0.85.

probe_patterns.description: Regular expressions replacing the built-in list of commands that only probe the container.

wait_patterns.description: Regular expressions for commands that wait on purpose (sleep, --watch, gh run watch by default): they count toward no repeat or failure rule.

integrator.description: ADR 0046: for the repositories listed, chargehand marks a finished task's pull request ready and merges it through the repository's required checks, and has a short session fix a failing required check, acting as a GitHub App (on GitLab, with the forge token). app_id and private_key_secret are both set or both left out: a profile that integrates GitLab projects only needs none. Unset: draft pull requests only, never touched again.

installation_id.description: Optional. chargehand asks GitHub which installation of the App covers each repository's owner (an App is installed once per account or organisation). This pins one installation, for the account it belongs to, and skips the lookup for that owner's repositories; it reaches no other owner.

private_key_secret.description: Secret item holding the App's private key (PEM). Never logged, never inside a container.

repositories.description: Per owner/repo (group/subgroup/project on GitLab): merge (marked ready, then auto-merge with squash, so the forge merges once the required checks pass) or ask (marked ready and commented on; a person merges). A repository not listed is off.

always_ask.description: Repositories that are ask whatever else says: this list wins over merge and over a repository not listed.

ci_fix.description: The session that fixes a failing required check on the pull request's branch. A key left out keeps its default.

max_attempts.description: Fix sessions per pull request, and never two for the same failing jobs. Default 3; 0: no fixer.

max_turns.description: Turn limit of one fix session. Default 20.

max_minutes.description: Wall clock of one fix session. Default 15.

wait_minutes.description: How long chargehand watches the required checks of one head commit before it stops; the task holds its slot meanwhile. Default 20.

forge.description: Which code host the remotes are on and how to reach it (ADR 0047). Unset: a remote on gitlab.com or on a host whose first label is gitlab is GitLab, and any other host is GitHub.

kind.description: The forge of every remote of this profile, whatever the host name says.

base_url.description: The API root: https://host/api/v4 for GitLab (the instance root https://host is accepted), https://host/api/v3 for GitHub Enterprise. Unset: derived from the remote's host (GitLab) or api.github.com.

token_secret.description: GitLab only: secret item for the API token (PRIVATE-TOKEN, scope api). Unset: push_secret, which then needs api and write_repository.

outside.description: A network besides the default one that the batch's egress container joins: the one the chargehand server sits on.

mcp_forward.description: host:port of the chargehand server as the egress container reaches it. Set, a session can call chargehand for research and review; unset, it cannot.

model_url.description: An Anthropic-compatible gateway as the egress container reaches it: http://host:port/path through a forward, or https://host/path through the proxy. Set, a session gets claude_code.api_key_secret (the key the gateway issued, with a budget) and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL instead of the real credential; unset, the real credential is in the container's environment.

otlp_url.description: An OTLP/HTTP collector as the egress container reaches it, http://host:port through a forward on a port no other forward uses. Set, each session's Claude Code exports its own logs and metrics there, tagged chargehand.run_id, chargehand.task_id, chargehand.task_run_id and chargehand.trace_id; unset, it exports nothing.

network.description: Hosts added to the preset's allowlist, and how a session reaches the chargehand server.

runner.description: The runner service in front of the container engine: one runner, named default (ADR 0058: runners lists several). Absent, and no runners: the server calls the engine itself (a laptop).

runners.description: ADR 0058: several runner services, in place of runner (never both). The server runs each task on the healthy runner with the most free memory that has a session slot, and keeps all of a task's sessions on it. A profile that names one runner behaves as one that uses runner.

name.description: Unique. It is in run events and in the driven-batch artifact.

url.description: The runner's address as the server reaches it.

api_key_secret.description: Secret item for the runner's bearer key.

max_sessions.description: Sessions this server runs on the runner at once. Unset: no limit besides max_parallel and max_parallel_total.

platform.description: The architecture of the runner's engine. Default linux/amd64. It picks the image: driven.image_variants.

weight.description: Multiplies the runner's free memory when two runners are compared. Default 1.

reserve_mb.description: Replaces driven.admission.reserve_mb for this runner: the memory left for everything else on its host.

workspace.description: shared (default): the runner reads the server's checkouts from a disk both see. bundle: the runner is not on the server's host, and the server sends it the repository as a git bundle.

forwards.description: The server's address as this runner's egress containers reach it. Each key replaces the same key of network for this runner; a key left out inherits it. A bundle runner needs mcp while network.mcp_forward is set, and model_url or otlp_url while network sets an http one.

outside.description: The network the egress container joins besides the batch's own. On a laptop engine: bridge.

image_variants.description: ADR 0058: for an image listed in images (services.images draws from the same list), the image to start on a runner of another platform. A runner uses the image as written unless this has an entry for its platform; a multi-platform index digest needs none.

push_secret.description: Secret item for the credential that pushes non-default branches and opens draft pull requests (on GitLab also merge requests, unless forge.token_secret names another).

task_source.description: How a tracker item id (a task's ref) becomes a goal: call the tool on the mcp_servers entry with {ref} replaced by the id, then read the goal from the JSON answer.

arguments.description: The tool's arguments; the string {ref} is replaced by the item id.

title.description: Dotted property names to the title string in the answer.

body.description: The same for the description; omit for a title-only goal.

automation.description: Work that starts without a caller (ADR 0051). Unset: nothing is watched.

github.description: A label on an issue, or a mention of the bot in a comment, by an allowed author starts a driven batch of one task; a reply to its questions continues it. chargehand polls GitHub as the GitHub App of driven.integrator, which also needs the Issues permission (read and write). Needs driven.enabled and driven.integrator.

path.description: The server's checkout of the repository (under repository_roots). A triggered batch starts from the commit its origin's default branch points at, after a fetch.

repositories.description: Per owner/repo: the repositories watched. Opt-in: a repository not listed is never read.

allowed_authors.description: GitHub logins whose label or comment starts a batch. Required, no default: an empty list means nothing triggers. For a label, the person who applied it must be on the list.

label.description: The label that triggers. Default chargehand.

mention.description: The mention that triggers in a comment. Default @chargehand.

poll_seconds.description: How often the repositories are read. Default 120.

budget_class.description: The size class of a triggered task whose issue has no size:S, size:M or size:L label (exactly one). It sets the governor's budget (ADR 0045). Default M.

max_tokens_total.description: The token cap of one triggered batch. Default 2000000.

max_usd_total.description: The dollar cap of one triggered batch, where the credential is priced. Default 5.

max_concurrent.description: Triggered batches running at once. A trigger over it waits for a slot, with one comment. Default 2.

max_starts_per_day.description: Triggered batches started in any 24 hours, answers included. A trigger over it is refused, with one comment. Default 10.

max_review_rounds.description: Review rounds per chargehand pull request: inline review comments of allowed authors, and comments that mention the bot, start a session on the pull request's branch. The CI fixer's attempts count against the same cap of 3 per pull request. Default 3; 0: the loop is off.

review_pulls.description: Review every open, non-draft pull request of the watched repositories, once per head commit, and comment the findings. Default false.

max_reviews_per_day.description: Reviews started in any 24 hours. A pull request over it waits until the window has room. Default 20.

repository_roots.description: Directories a request's repository may sit under; the worker reads a clone of it under worker_root (ADR 0023). "/" allows any repository. Default: worker_root alone; the CLI's run also allows the directory it was launched in (ADR 0028).

intake_model.description: Default (ADR 0026): unset — intake runs on the runtime's own default model.

run_cap_usd.description: Hard cap per run in USD; the worker is interrupted above it (ADR 0011). Default 1.00.

max_parallel_nodes.description: Worker nodes of one run that may run at once (ADR 0011 allows 2 per model). 1 keeps one worker process at a time on a host short on memory. Default 2.

run_log.description: Path of the JSONL run log. Default runs/run-log.jsonl (gitignored) in a checkout, else chargehand/run-log.jsonl under the per-user data directory.

usage_on_spans.description: Put tokens and cost on call spans (ADR 0021). Only for calls no gateway records, e.g. Claude Code on a subscription; with a LiteLLM gateway leave false (ADR 0012).

prices.description: USD per 1M tokens, keyed by provider/model. cache_write includes the provider's surcharge. Default (ADR 0026): empty — every PriceUsd lookup is unknown cost until a model is priced here.

models.description: Maps the placeholder models presets name (e.g. provider/worker-model) to your provider/model ids. An unmapped placeholder uses the runtime's default model.

http.description: chargehand serve: HTTP and MCP, on 127.0.0.1 unless listen opens it (ADR 0018, ADR 0024).

listen.description: IP address to bind. Anything but loopback needs allowed_hosts, and belongs on a private network only (ADR 0024).

allowed_hosts.description: Host names accepted besides localhost and 127.0.0.1, e.g. the server's private-network name.

max_concurrent_runs.description: Runs the server executes at once (a driven batch counts as one). Default 1, one at a time, as ADR 0011's per-model limit assumes; raise it only when the model's rate limit allows.

api_key_secret.description: Secret-store item holding the API key every caller sends as a bearer token. It opens the implicit owner account: every run, no caps.

ui.description: Serve the web UI at /ui/ (ADR 0054) and the operator console at /console/ (ADR 0056): static files, no key needed to load them; the page signs in with an API key and calls the same routes. Off by default.

accounts.description: Accounts besides the owner (ADR 0050). Their keys come from `chargehand accounts add <name>`, stored as salted hashes in accounts.json beside the run log; a key of an account removed here opens nothing. An account lists, reads and cancels only its own runs; it never halts the server.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Recorded as `actor` on the account's runs, results and events.

max_usd_per_day.description: Dollars the account's runs may cost in a UTC day, by their results' usage. Counts priced runs only; a subscription run adds none, so pair it with a token cap.

max_usd_per_month.description: The same over a UTC calendar month.

max_tokens_per_day.description: Input plus output tokens in a UTC day.

max_tokens_per_month.description: Input plus output tokens in a UTC calendar month.

max_concurrent_runs.description: Unfinished runs (queued or running) the account may have at once.

driven.description: Whether the account may start a batch (a request with a driven block). A batch pushes branches and opens pull requests with the server's credential.

repositories.description: Absolute directories the account's context.repository.path may be, or be below. Absent: any repository the server allows.

model.description: The account's own model credential (ADR 0053): its read-only runs and its batches use it instead of the server's, and are priced as API usage. Needs the claude_code runtime. A subscription token is the owner's and is not accepted here.

api_key_secret.description: Secret-store item holding an Anthropic API key, or the key a gateway issued when base_url names that gateway.

base_url.description: An Anthropic-compatible gateway's base URL (http or https, no credentials, query or fragment). Absent: Anthropic's own API.

allow_server_credential.description: An account with no model block may spend the server's model credential. Default false: its runs are refused with model_credential_missing. The owner always uses the server's.

mcp_servers.description: MCP servers by name (ADR 0034), for memory providers and preset services to refer to. Nothing connects until something refers to a server. Each has exactly one of url and command. {secret:item} is allowed in header and environment values only: it is resolved through the secrets chain when the connection opens, and a server whose secret no source resolves is not connected.

url.description: A server reached over HTTP. Streamable HTTP or, for older servers, SSE (see transport). Never holds {secret:...}: put a credential in headers.

transport.description: auto tries Streamable HTTP, then falls back to SSE if the server does not support it. Name sse for a server that only speaks the older SSE transport (skips the failed first attempt), or streamable-http to never fall back. A worker granted this server through a preset's services gets Streamable HTTP for auto, since its runtime cannot fall back: name sse for an SSE-only server.

headers.description: Headers sent with every request, e.g. { "Authorization": "Bearer {secret:item}" }.

command.description: A stdio server's argv, started by chargehand. Never holds {secret:...}: put a credential in env.

env.description: Environment of the stdio server, on top of the SDK's default set (PATH, HOME and the like). Nothing else of chargehand's own environment is inherited.

preset_services.description: Services by preset name (ADR 0034): the MCP servers of mcp_servers whose tools that preset's workers may call. A list here replaces the preset's own services, so a shipped read-only preset such as incident gets this profile's logs, metrics and traces servers without a private copy of the preset file. Explicit tool names only: a glob is allowed, a bare * is not. Workers stay read-only whatever a server offers.

prompt_enhancer.description: A prompt enhancer (ADR 0040), unset by default: an entry of mcp_servers that lists the tools enhance and feedback (whetstone's contract). A client sends it the prompt and the repository, commit, task kind and client name, shows the rewrite beside the original and sends the original unless the user accepts it; the outcome goes back through feedback. A slow, failing or unreachable enhancer means the original is sent.

deadline_ms.description: How long to wait for enhance before sending the original; default 1500. Also the deadline_ms the enhancer is told.

memory.description: Long-term memory (ADR 0034): an ordered list of providers, each an entry of mcp_servers plus a declarative mapping from chargehand's recall and retain to that server's tools. Each executed run asks every provider at once, each under its own timeout, and gives the merged facts to its nodes as unverified context labelled with the provider's name. The single-object form (backend, url, namespace) was removed; a profile that still has it fails to load.

memoryProvider.description: One memory provider. Its position in the list is its priority.

name.description: Unique in the list. The label on the provider's facts in the prompt, and in the run log and traces.

namespace.description: The value of {namespace} in the tool arguments, e.g. a Hindsight bank. Default: name. Leave it out for a server with no banks.

tools.description: The server's tools that give the provider its operations. recall is required; retain is required when retain is true; invalidate is optional and no run calls it.

max_facts.description: Facts kept per recall (default 10). Also the value of {max_facts}.

max_chars.description: Characters kept per recall, all facts together (default 4000).

max_fact_chars.description: Characters kept per fact; a longer one is cut with an ellipsis (default 600).

timeout_seconds.description: How long one recall or retain call may take before the provider is skipped (default 10).

retain.description: Write to this provider after a run: the claims whose file or commit citations resolved, with their locators, the repository and the commit; never the request or the summary. Needs tools.retain; a provider without one is recall-only.

arguments.description: The tool's arguments, as a template. A string that is exactly one placeholder is replaced by the value with its type ({tags} an array, {max_facts} an integer, {timestamp} an ISO 8601 string) and a null value drops the argument; a placeholder inside longer text is replaced as text; numbers and booleans are literal. Placeholders: recall {query} {namespace} {max_facts}; retain {namespace} {text} {context} {document_id} {timestamp} {tags}; invalidate {namespace} {id} {reason}. An unknown placeholder fails at load.

results.description: Recall only: how to read the answer. Without this block, the answer's results array is read and each element's id and text fields. A block that leaves out path reads the root.

path.description: Dotted property names leading to the array of results in the answer (structuredContent, else the first text block parsed as JSON). Empty: the answer itself is the array.

id.description: The property of each element that holds its id. A missing id becomes a hash of the text.

text.description: What makes a fact from an element (default "text"): a property name, a template over its properties ("{date}: {summary}"), or an ordered list of these. An entry is used only if every property it names is present and non-empty; the first that is used wins, and an element with none is skipped.

format.description: text takes the whole first text block of the answer as one fact and ignores path, id and text.
